chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both.
That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a sheep that died and milk was drawn from it, so he said: 'That is pure haram.'

This is a singular narration (shadh) narrated only by Wahb ibn Wahb, and he is very weak among the hadith scholars. And if it were sound, it would be permissible that the reason for it was a form of taqiyya (dissimulation), because it agrees with the opinions of the general public (Ahl al-Sunnah), for they forbid everything from the dead animal (maytah) and do not permit its use in any manner.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on milk from a dead animal in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this singular report from Wahb ibn Wahb, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) declared milk from a dead sheep as 'pure haram,' a ruling that aligns with the general consensus (jumhur) of Sunni scholars who prohibit all parts of the maytah. Shaykh al-Tusi notes the narrator's weakness but suggests the ruling may reflect taqiyya, allowing for practical flexibility while maintaining the appearance of strict prohibition. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where milk, being a flowing fluid distinct from the solid carcass, might be considered pure even if the animal is dead, though Ali's statement emphasizes the prohibition aspect.
